physical_harm: Death of the victim, injuries to the deceased and to the witnesses
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the accused entered the house armed with the intention of committing robbery
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the accused, who were armed, entered the house of the victims at midnight with the intention of committing robbery and that A-2 stabbed the deceased on the abdomen and thighs, causing his death.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, including P.W. 1 to 4, and relied on their testimony to establish the sequence of events and the injuries caused to the deceased and others.
post_offence_conduct: The accused were overpowered by the neighbours, tied up with a rope, and information was sent to the police. The accused were brought to the ground floor and later apprehended.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 20th/21st November, 1991; Trial judgment: 11.12.2003; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: December 14, 2010
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: I. Venkatanarayana, Ramesh Allanki, D. Mahesh Babu; Counsel for the State: Anil Kumar Tandale, Manoj C. Mishra, Brajesh Jha
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted under Sections 302/34, 460 and 324 of the Indian Penal Code; High Court: Converted conviction under Section 302 to Section 304 Part I; Supreme Court: Set aside High Court's judgment and restored trial court's judgment
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the two accused, who were armed, entered the house of the victims at midnight with the intention of committing robbery. They caused fatal injuries to the deceased and also injured other witnesses, which indicates a clear intention to cause death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no common intention on the part of the accused to commit murder. They claimed that the deceased's death was an unfortunate accident resulting from the accused's attempt to extricate themselves from the deceased's grip during a scuffle.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the common intention to commit murder can be inferred from the circumstances of the case, even if it arises during an incident, and that the initial purpose of robbery does not preclude the intention to cause death if the accused used weapons effectively.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court's observation that the matter fell under Section 304 Part I and not Section 302 of the IPC was found to be erroneous. The trial court's conviction under Sections 302/34, 460 and 324 was restored.
